gaps.sentence: She ___ three novels since she retired.
gaps.explanation: 'Since she retired' (up to now) — present perfect.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: We ___ each other since primary school.
gaps.explanation: 'Since primary school' — present perfect of a state verb.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: Shakespeare ___ thirty-seven plays that we know of.
gaps.hint: a dead historical figure, finished lifetime
gaps.explanation: Actions of people who are no longer alive take the past simple even without a time phrase: wrote.

gaps.sentence: I ___ coffee at all, but I drink tea every morning.
gaps.hint: a general habit contrasted with another habit
gaps.explanation: A permanent habit takes the present simple, so the negative form is: don't drink.

gaps.sentence: I ___ from Tom since March, which is starting to worry me.
gaps.hint: since March continuing into the present
gaps.explanation: 'Since March' up to now takes the present perfect: haven't heard.

gaps.sentence: The bus ___ at 6.40 tomorrow morning, according to the timetable.
gaps.hint: official timetables use the present simple
gaps.explanation: Official timetables take the present simple for future events: leaves.
